unresolved_added: Amazon market value and review volume are background claims, not a frozen source dataset.
The source alternates among rating, sentiment, reputation, product success, and sales without a single outcome dictionary.
Star ratings are ordinal observations; Gaussian vector coordinates do not establish calibrated probabilities.
The claim that the VEC mapping is one-to-one does not prove the smoothed vector preserves meaningful ordinal distances.
Product rating proportions do not identify technological complexity as the reason for lower ratings.
The five assumptions suppress marketplace shocks, customer heterogeneity, delayed reviews, and intervention changes without sensitivity tests.
Treating reviews as authentic customer feeling ignores spam, selection, coordinated reviews, and strategic rating behavior.
The 80/20 split is stated, but the split unit, random seed, and temporal leakage control are not frozen.
One group member manually annotates seed words; inter-rater agreement and annotation protocol are absent.
Low-frequency emotion words are discarded without a support threshold or rare-event analysis.
Five-class labels are aligned to stars by analogy, not by a held-out calibration table.
Treating an entire short review as one context can lose sentence boundaries, negation scope, and sarcasm.
Gaussian word distance assumes proximity means semantic relevance and leaves sigma calibration incomplete.
Context vectors mix review length and vocabulary dimension without a stated scaling or truncation rule.
KL divergence requires positive probabilities and smoothing details that are not reported.
The symmetric KL sum is not shown to be a metric or robust to zero-probability entries.
Averaging word similarities gives every candidate equal influence despite repetitions and syntax.
CE group averages can be changed by seed-group size and class imbalance.
VADER's extended lexicon can inherit annotation leakage from the CE seed list.
The equal fusion coefficient lambda=0.5 is asserted rather than tuned or cross-validated.
Softmax smooths scores but does not establish probability calibration.
The argmax class discards uncertainty and near-ties in the five-vector.
Product title/parent/id differences below 0.01% do not prove exact interchangeability for every row.
Removing marketplace as a field assumes the US source has no useful platform variation.
Helpful votes are exposure- and popularity-biased and need not mean factual usefulness.
Cosine agreement between text and star vectors is not a measure of review truth or quality.
The importance entropy sign is difficult to reconcile with the conclusion's claim about moderately rated high-entropy reviews.
The top one percent cutoff is arbitrary and its stability is tested only through a ranking distance.
DTW similarity of rankings is not normalized by a null permutation or tied to a decision threshold.
The data sizes for the three products differ greatly, making ranking and error comparisons uneven.
The reputation growth equation treats text class argmax and star rating as commensurate after weighting.
The rolling window t0=10 is selected from a 90-day feedback statement without a sensitivity curve.
The negative threshold k3=2, k1, and k2 are not estimated from observed complaint outcomes.
The sigmoid penalty encodes a social-behavior story without direct behavioral validation.
Negative comments can dominate the penalty even when their reporting rate differs by product.
Reputation bounds, clipping, negative growth handling, and initial conditions are not fully specified.
Figure 6/7 visual trajectories are not accompanied by raw series, uncertainty bands, or replication seeds.
The reported k1 robustness and k2 sensitivity do not imply robust product ranking or launch decisions.
The Summary maximum RMSE 0.131 conflicts with the body validation maximum 0.031.
The AR order p=50 is large relative to the visible time series and lacks regularization or order selection evidence.
The chronological three-quarters/one-quarter split is a single validation design, not external validation.
Recursive AR forecasts can compound errors over the stated future horizon.
White-noise notation is included without residual diagnostics.
Historical average and future average use intervals whose endpoint and integration convention are not fully defined.
The gamma sign/magnitude flowchart does not show numeric class thresholds or tie handling.
Weak/strong success and failure labels have no external business or safety calibration.
The forecast verdicts for three products are conditional on the reputation construction and AR extrapolation.
One- and five-star focus is justified by correlations and literature but may discard informative moderate reviews.
Consecutive-rating run length x is set to 10 for two products and 5 for microwave without a common selection rule.
Smaller x mechanically raises observed event frequency, so cross-product comparisons can be threshold-driven.
Post-run rating gaps are observational and cannot establish that a run incited reviews.
The table's reputation labels and frequency comparisons lack uncertainty intervals.
The monthly hair-dryer example is one product and cannot establish a universal extreme-rating mechanism.
Bayes word probabilities use raw frequencies without smoothing, stop-word control, or dependence correction.
The top ten word table may be dominated by product names, boilerplate, negation, or review-length artifacts.
Word-rating associations are not causal descriptors of product quality.
Extracting keywords from the top one percent and counting them in all reviews mixes selected and full-corpus denominators.
Feature groups and keyword dictionaries are not fully released or independently reproducible.
Pacifier size/safety, microwave price/features, and hair-dryer power/noise are descriptive preferences, not willingness-to-pay estimates.
Counting 13 hair-dryer danger reports in the top 100 does not estimate product hazard incidence.
Launch timing recommendations do not include inventory, cost, legal, safety, or market-share constraints.
Recommendations to increase promotion after five-star runs can encourage manipulation or selective visibility.
Real-time collection of informative reviews needs a monitoring cadence, alert threshold, and staffing rule.
The memo reports `strong accuracy` and broad generalization despite limited released inputs and validation.
The company letter compresses conditional model outputs into direct timing advice without all uncertainty qualifiers.
The source claims novelty without a systematic comparison against sentiment, rating, or time-series baselines.
The source claims robustness while omitting morphology, lexicon, lambda, window, AR-order, and forecast-horizon sensitivity.
Manual annotation cost is acknowledged but no active-learning or multi-annotator repair is supplied.
Failure to recognize inflections and plurals can systematically alter sentiment classes.
Omitted marketing strategies are acknowledged but their absence can confound rating/reputation trends.
Appendix A seed words and Appendix B counts are implementation evidence, not reusable author prose.
Appendix C customer reviews are third-party text and must never enter anti-copy or human-style positive counts.
Appendix D-I code snippets are incomplete without data paths, versions, seeds, and runtime environment.
Figures, tables, formulas, code, watermarks, and QR furniture must remain outside positive-language counts while still binding model/visual evidence.
Every claim that a product will succeed, fail, or benefit from a strategy must be labeled as conditional on the source data, model, horizon, and missing validation.
